q_en: Who introduced Vernacular Press Act in 1878, which subjected newspapers published in Indian languages to a censorship?

After this, the government kept regular track of the vernacular newspapers. Viceroy, Lord Rippon (1880-1884) repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882. Vernacular Press Act (1878) was aimed to cripple regional language newspapers that print against the government by seizing their printing presses.

The Mundaka Upanishad is an ancient Sanskrit Vedic text, embedded inside Atharva Veda. Upon independence of India, Satyameva Jayate was adopted as the national motto of India It is inscribed in Devanagari script at the base of the national emblem. q_en: Evidence of the earliest ploughed field from the Harappan Civilisation was found at _______.

Most Harappan sites are located in semi-arid lands, where irrigation was probably required for agriculture.

q_en: Which is the hottest planet in our solar system with a surface temperature of over 450 degrees Celsius?

The Universities of Calcutta and Bombay (now Mumbai) were formed in July 1857 and Madras (now Chennai) in September 1857, followed by Punjab in 1882, and Allahabad University in 1887.

q_en: Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Hydaspes. Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of Hydaspes. The Battle is called the “Battle of Hydaspes” named after the Hydaspes (Jhelum) River in Greek. The battle was fought in 326 BC with the king of the Paurava dynasty, located on the banks of the Vitasta (Jhelum) river in the Punjab region. In 326 BC, Alexander invaded India, after crossing the river Indus he advanced towards Taxila.

q_en: ______ of the Indian Constitution contains the Fundamental Duties.
e_en: The correct answer is Part IV A. Fundamental Duties The original constitution did not contain any provisions related to Fundamental Duties. This section was added through the 42nd amendment act to the constitution of India. It was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. These were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution Originally 10 in number, one more duty was added through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

q_en: ______ is a famous dance form of Jammu and Kashmir.
e_en: The correct answer is Dumhal. Dumhal The Dumhal dance is one of the most prominent folk dances in Jammu & Kashmir, India. In the Wattal tribe, the Dumhal dance is performed on certain occasions. The dancers' tunes are folk melodies that they sing in a chorus. The men hold a banner, gather in a procession, and march to a designated area. They arrive at a specific area and plant the flag on the earth. The Dumhal dance is then performed which revolves around the banner.

q_en: Bhanu ______ is a festival dedicated to the worship of the Sun God.
e_en: The correct answer is Saptami. Bhanu Saptami It is devoted to the Lord Surya (Sun God).</

q_en: In which of the following places did the Indian National Congress hold its special session in September 1920?
e_en: The correct answer is Calcutta. Congress held a special session in Calcutta in September 1920 under the presidentship of Lala Lajpat Rai. It met to pass the resolution of the Non-Cooperation Movement. Mahatma Gandhi wrongly predicted that if the non-cooperation movement gets successful, Swaraj could be attained in one year. The Non-cooperation movement was launched in 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi with the aim of Swaraj (self-governance). However, the movement was not successful.

q_en: According to the Central Pollution Control Board of India, particulate sizes of diameter ______ micrometres are responsible for causing the greatest harm to human health.
e_en: The correct answer is option D. Particulate matter refers to tiny particles suspended in the air which have diameter of 2.5 microns(2.5*10⁻⁶ m) or less are called PM₂.₅. These are visible only with the help of an electron microscope. These are so small that they can easily enter the lungs and subsequently into blood. Once inhaled they can cause respiratory and heart problems. Sources: burning of fossil fuels like coal, wood and forest fires.

q_en: Any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than ______ years is under the category of Culturable Wasteland.
e_en: The correct answer is five. Culturable wasteland refers to the land which is not cultivated for more than five years in sequence. This land has the potential to grow crops but was left unused for any reason.

q_en: Gaumukh Kund is a reservoir located in which of the following forts?
e_en: The correct answer is Chittorgarh. Gaumukh Kund is a sacred water body situated on the western part of the famous Chittorgarh Fort. 'Gaumukh' literally means the 'mouth of a cow'. The water flows through the cracks in the rocks and in due course, falls into the reservoir. The Chittorgarh Fort is also known as Chittorgarh or Chittor Fort. Chittorgarh Fort is the largest fort in India and Asia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q_en: Who is the author of the novel 'A Passage to India'?
e_en: The correct answer is EM Forster. * A Passage to India* (1924) is a novel by English author E. M. Forster set against the backdrop of the British Raj and the Indian independence movement in the 1920s. It was selected as one of the 100 great works of 20th-century English literature by the *Modern Library* and won the 1924 James Tait Black Memorial Prize for fiction. Time magazine included the novel in its "All Time 100 Novels" list.

q_en: Arunima Sinha was the first ______ female to scale Mount Everest.
e_en: The correct answer is female amputee. Arunima Sinha was the world's first female amputee to scale Mount Everest. She was also the world's first female amputee to scale Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Elbrus, Mount Kosciusko, Mount Aconcagua, Carstensz Pyramid, and Mount Vinson. Arunima Sinha was awarded the Padma Shri award in 2015 and Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award in 2015.

q_en: The Bihari Puraskar is one of the three literary awards instituted by the ______ in 1991.
e_en: The correct answer is KK Birla Foundation. Bihari Puraskar is a literary award instituted by K. K. Birla Foundation in 1991. The award is one of the three literary awards instituted by the K.K. Birla Foundation in 1991. The award is named after the famous Hindi poet Bihari and is awarded to an outstanding work published in Hindi or Rajasthani by a Rajasthani writer in the last 10 years. It carries a citation, a plaque, and prize money of Rs. 2.5 lakh.

q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with Right to Freedom of Religion?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 25 to 28. The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed by Articles 25 to 28 of the constitution of India. Article 25: Religious freedom of conscience and freedom of profession, practice, and dissemination. Article 26: Freedom to manage religious affairs Article 27: Right to pay taxes to support any other religion. Article 28: Freedom of participation in religious instruction or religious worship in some institutions of education.

q_en: Lord Buddha was born in ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Lumbini, Nepal. Gautam Buddha was born in 563 BC on the Vaishakha Poornima Day at Lumbini (near Kapilavastu) in Nepal. He left his palace at 29 in search of truth (also called ‘Mahabhinishkramana’ or The Great Renunciation). Attained ‘ Nirvana ’ or ‘Enlightenment’ at 35 at Gaya in Magadha (Bihar) under the Pipal tree. Delivered the first sermon at Sarnath. His first sermon is called ‘Dharmachakrapravartan’ or ‘Turning of the Wheel of Law’.

q_en: Kanch Mahal is located in which of the following districts?
e_en: The correct answer is Agra. Kanch Mahal is situated close to Akbar’s tomb in Sikandra (Agra district). Built by Jahangir and was used as a royal hunting lodge. The square-shaped Kanch Mahal is a testimony to the best features of domestic Mughal architecture. Records show that the Mahal was built from 1605 to 1619. It is called Kanch Mahal because of the abundant use of tile work in its construction.

q_en: In which year was the All India Kisan Sabha founded in Lucknow with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as the president?
e_en: The correct answer is 1936. ​ The All India Kisan Sabha was formed in 1936 at Lucknow. All India Kisan Sabha is also known as ‘Akhil Bhartiya Kisan Sabha.’ Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was the President of the Sabha. The secretary of All India Kisan Sabha was NG Ranga. The motives of the All India Kisan Sabha were: To abolish the Zamindari system, To reduce land revenue, To institutionalize credit.

q_en: As per India Census 2011, which of the following states has the least growth of population in percentage terms between 2001 to 2011?
e_en: The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh. The population of Himachal Pradesh grew by 12.94% during the 2001-11 census while Punjab, Haryana, and Uttarakhand respectively 13.89%, 19.90%, and 18.81%. The total population of Himachal Pradesh was 6,864,602 according to the 2011 Census and the literacy rate was 82.80.

q_en: Which of the following Indian personalities holds the honour of being the first-ever Indian to perform in the prestigious Royal Albert Hall, London?
e_en: The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar. Lata Mangeshkar was the first Indian artist to perform live at London’s iconic Royal Albert Hall in 1974. She was a legendary singer, who passed away aged 92 in Mumbai on 6 Feb 2022. Famous Song: Ae Mere Wattan Ke Logo (Written by Kavi Pradeep and sang on Republic Day 26 January 1963), Aisa Des Hai Mera (Veer-Zaara), Aaja Re Pardesi (Madhumati), Inhin Logon Ne (Pakeezah), Aayega Aanewala (Mahal), etc.

q_en: Which of the following states is known for Mando Festival?
e_en: The correct answer is Goa. Mando Festival is celebrated in Goa. Mando Festival Mando, in the early nineteenth century, was a song written almost exclusively in the spirit of competition. It was a poetic and musical expression of a personal feeling or an allegorical description of a political or level episode. Its theme is usually of love - bitter and sweet passion which is in slow and deliberate motion and is well expressed through beautiful movements of words and dance.

q_en: Which of the following states shares the longest land border with Bangladesh?
e_en: The correct answer is West Bengal. There are five Indian states that share their boundary with Bangladesh. They are - West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Indian shares the longest boundary with Bangladesh of about 4096 km.

q_en: Which of the following French travelers, who wrote accounts of what he saw, frequently comparing India with the situation in Europe, was closely associated with the Mughal court, as a physician to Prince Dara Shikoh?
e_en: The correct answer is Francois Bernier. Francois Bernier ​He was a French traveler. He visited India during the reign of Shah Jahan. He was closely associated with the Mughal court, as a physician to Prince Dara Shikoh and later was attached to the court of Aurangzeb. He wrote the book 'Travels in the Mughal Empire'.​

q_en: Which of the following cities lies on the bank of the river Gomti?
e_en: The correct answer is Lucknow. Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, lies on the bank of the river Gomti. Besides Lucknow, other towns located on its banks are Lakhimpur Kheri, Sultanpur, and Jaunpur. The Gomti river provides drinking water to these cities. Gomti The Gomti, a monsoon- and groundwater-fed river, have its origin at Gomat Taal (earlier known as Fulhaar jheel) near Madho Tanda, Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh.

q_en: 'Lal Salaam', a novel on the story of a young officer and of the challenges he faces against a system that is steeped in backroom politics and corruption is written by whom among the following Union Ministers?
e_en: The correct answer is Smriti Zubin Irani. Union Minister Smriti Zubin Irani has turned author with her first novel Lal Salaam. The novel, inspired by the tragic killings of 76 CRPF personnel in Dantewada in April 2010, is a tribute to the exceptional men and women who have given a lifetime of service to the country. The book hit the stands on 29 November 2021. Lal Salaam is the story of a young officer, Vikram Pratap Singh.

q_en: The first Khelo India University Games were organised in which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha. Khelo India University Games (2020) After the resounding success of the Khelo India School Games in 2018 and the Youth Games in 2019 and 2020, for the very first time, the Khelo India University Games were held in 2020 in Odisha. It was held in the Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology, Odisha. This was the largest ever competition held at the university level in India.

q_en: In 1928, who wrote the Congress Party's Nehru Report, a future constitution for independent India based on the grating of dominion status?
e_en: The correct answer is Motilal Nehru. Nehru Report (1928) Nehru Report 1928 was a report by a committee headed by Pt. Motilal Nehru. This committee was created when Lord Birkenhead, Secretary of State of India, asked the Indian leaders to draft a constitution for the country. The report which demanded a Dominion Status for India was considered by Congress.

q_en: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 years to _____ years.
e_en: The correct answer is 18. The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 In India, the voting age has been reduced from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988. It comes into force by amending Article 326. The bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 15th December 1988. The bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 20th December 1988. The bill was assented to by then-President R. Venkataraman on 28th March 1989. The bill came into force on 28th March 1989.

q_en: Ozone layer in the atmosphere shields the surface of the Earth from which radiation from the Sun?
e_en: The correct answer is Ultraviolet (UV) light. Ozone layer It is a layer of ozone molecules found in the stratosphere (the second layer of the atmosphere). Ozone is a molecule made up of three oxygen atoms, often referenced as O3. The ozone layer is typically thicker over the poles than over the equator. The ozone layer exists in the stratosphere, a layer 10 to 50 km above the Earth’s surface.

q_en: The Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) was established in the year ______.
e_en: The correct answer is 1970. The Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) was established on 31st July 1970 as a Government Company registered under the Companies Act 1956. In the initial period of setting up, as an agency in the Public Sector, a Corporation was charged with the responsibility of equitable distribution of cotton among the different constituents of the industry and to serve as a vehicle for the canalization of imports of cotton.

q_en: Based on archaeological findings, which of the following dances is believed to be the oldest of the surviving Indian classical dances?
e_en: The correct answer is Odissi. Based on archaeological findings, Odissi is believed to be the oldest of the surviving Indian classical dances. Odissi is indigenous to Orissa in eastern India. It is predominantly a dance for women, with postures that replicate those found in temple sculptures. Odissi is a very complex and expressive dance, with over fifty mudras (symbolic hand gestures) commonly used.</strong&g

q_en: Who among the following was given the title of 'Khan-e-Khana' by Akbar?
e_en: The correct answer is Mirza Abdul Rahim Khan. Akbar gave the title of 'Khan-e-Khana' to Mirza Abdul Rahim Khan. Khanzada Mirza Khan Abdul Rahim was the real name of Rahim. He was one of the nine important ministers in his court, also known as the Navaratnas. The Navaratnas of Akbar were as follows: Raja Birbal, Tansen, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Man Singh, Raja Todar Mal, Mullah Do Piaza, Fakir Aziao-Din, Abdul Rahim Khan-e-Khana.

q_en: Which of the following does NOT come under the purview of 'paper taxes'?
e_en: The correct answer is Excise tax.

q_en: Under which Article of the Constitution of India can the President of India declare National Emergency if he/she feels that there is a grave threat to the security of the country?
e_en: The correct answer is 352. Article 352 states that the President can proclaim an Emergency if he/she believes that a “grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion” only on the written recommendation of the cabinet. The 44th Constitutional Amendment of India replaced the term ‘internal disturbance’ with ‘armed rebellion’.

q_en: Who among the following is the author of 'The Turbulent Years : 1980 - 1996'?
e_en: The correct answer is Pranab Mukherjee. Pranab Mukherjee is the author of The Turbulent Years : 1980 - 1996. His other books are 'Thoughts and Reflections', 'Beyond Survival'. Pranab Kumar Mukherjee was an Indian politician who served as the 13th president of India from 2012 until 2017.

q_en: Which of the following states/union territories is NOT touched by the Aravalli Range?
e_en: The correct answer is Punjab. The Aravalli Range is a mountain range in Northwestern India, the length of the range is approximately 692 km in a southwest direction. The Aravalli range starts from Delhi, passing through southern Haryana and Rajasthan, and ending in Gujarat. Hence, it does not pass through Punjab. The literal meaning of the Aravalli Range is ‘line of peaks’.

q_en: Articles 124 and 217 of the Constitution of India deal with which of the following?
o_en: The appointment of the UPSC Chairman
The appointment of the Chief Minister
e_en: The correct answer is The appointment of judges. Articles 124 and 217 of the Constitution deal with the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and high courts. Article 124 states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and such number of other judges not being less than seven as Parliament may by law prescribe.

q_en: ''Yakshagana' is popular form of dance-drama of :
e_en: The correct answer is Southern India. Yakshagana is a traditional theater form of Karnataka. Its literal meaning is 'Yaksha's song'. It developed in the Udupi district of Karnataka. Its origin is believed to be between the 10th and 16th centuries. It is a temple art form depicting mythological stories, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata, the Bhagavata, and other Hindu epics. It is strongly influenced by the Vaishnava Bhakti movement.

q_en: Who was the Viceroy of India at the times of the Dandi March initiated by Gandhiji?
e_en: The correct answer is Lord Irwin.

q_en: In which of the following states is the headquarters of NSDL Payments Bank situated?
e_en: The correct answer is Maharashtra.

q_en: Which of the following Indian states is home to the largest population of the greater one-horned rhinoceros?
e_en: The correct answer is Assam. <u

q_en: In which of the following years was the Battle of Imphal won?
e_en: The correct answer is 1944.

q_en: 'Dalkhai' dance is associated with the state of :
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha.

q_en: After West Bengal, with which of the following Indian states does Bangladesh have the common longest border?
e_en: The correct answer is Tripura. India and Bangladesh share a 4,096 km long international border, the fifth-longest land border in the world, with West Bengal having the highest length with 2,217 km. The length of the border in the other four states is Tripura(856km), Meghalaya(443km), Assam(262km), and Mizoram(180km). Hence, Tripura is the correct answer.

q_en: Deomali mountain peak is in :
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha. The Deomali (1672m) mountain peak is situated on the Eastern Ghat in Odisha. It is the highest peak of Odisha. Deomali is a mountain peak in the Chandragiri-Pottangi subrange of the Eastern Ghats. It is located near Koraput town in the Koraput district of southern Odisha, India.

q_en: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Three Khans: And the Emergence of New India'?
e_en: The correct answer is Kaveree Bamzai. “The Three Khans: And the Emergence of New India” is written by Kaveree Bamzai. Kaveree Bamzai is an Indian journalist, author, and film critic.

q_en: ITNS Challan Number ________ is used for payment of Fringe Benefit Tax.
e_en: The correct answer is 283.

q_en: _______ was land granted to a Brahmana, who was usually exempted from paying land revenue and other dues to the king, and was often given the right to collect these dues.
e_en: The correct answer is An agrahara. Agrahara in Sanskrit refers to “land exempt from leasing rights”. Agrahara was land, village, or fields that were given to Brahmaṇas. The Agraharas were exempted from taxes and had other administrative immunities. Agrahara was also known as Agraharam, Chaturvedimangalams, Ghatoka, and Boya in ancient times. Agraharas were built and maintained by dynasties like Cholas and Pallavas.

q_en: Who among the following made the statement: "one caste, one religion, one god for humankind"?
e_en: The correct answer is Shri Narayana Guru. Shri Narayana Guru, a guru from the Ezhava caste in present-day Kerala proclaimed the ideals of unity for his people. He argued against treating people unequally on the basis of caste differences. According to him, all humankind belonged to the same caste. "Oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (One caste, one religion, one god for humankind) is one of his famous statements.

q_en: On the eve of which of the following festivals is Kotappakonda Fair of Andhra Pradesh organised?
e_en: The correct answer is Maha Shivaratri. Sri Trikoteswara Swamy temple at Kotappakonda hill is one of the ancient and most famous temples in the district. Lakhs of devotees visit the temple and participate in the two-day fair during the Maha Shivaratri festival. The highlight of the festival is the presence of lofty illuminated ‘prabhalu,’ made of bamboo and decorated with coloured cloth and paper. Some of them are as tall as 60-70 feet and are carried on bullock carts.

q_en: The Composition of the Council of States comes under the purview of which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
e_en: The correct answer is 80. The Rajya Sabha or Council of States is the upper house of the Parliament of India. Composition/Strength of Rajya Sabha: Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250. Out of 250 seats of Rajya Sabha, 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the two Union Territories.

q_en: Who among the following has become the Head of the National Steering Committee formed by the Ministry of Education for the development of National Curriculum Framework?
e_en: The correct answer is K Kasturirangan. The Ministry of Education has formed the National Steering Committee for the development of National Curriculum Frameworks on 21 September 2021. The committee will be chaired by K Kasturirangan. The committee will develop four National Curriculum Frameworks- including the National Curriculum Framework for School Education, and National Curriculum for Early Childhood Care and Education.

q_en: Whose autobiography is titled 'A Century is Not Enough: My Roller-coaster Ride to Success'?
e_en: The correct answer is Sourav Ganguly. A Century is Not Enough: My Roller-coaster Ride to Success (2018) is an English autobiography written by former Indian cricketer and captain Sourav Ganguly. Sourav Ganguly was the former President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. He is known as <span style="font-w

q_en: When do we celebrate National Press Day in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 16 November. National Press Day is observed on the 16th of November. This was the day on which the Press Council of India started functioning as a moral watchdog.

q_en: In which of the following years did the Government of India appoint the Saddler University Commission to analyse the problems of the Calcutta University?
e_en: The correct answer is 1917. Saddler Commission was set up in 1917 to study and report on problems of Calcutta University. It analysed the conditions prevailing in the educational system and suggested some measures, submitting its report in 1919. It recommended a separate board for secondary and intermediate education It stated that the improvement of secondary education was a necessary condition for the improvement of University education.

q_en: The presiding deity of the Dakshineswar Temple in Kolkata is Goddess _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Bhavatarini Kali. The presiding deity of Dakshineswar temple is Bhavatarini Kali, a form of Adi Parashakti Kali. The temple is one of the holiest places in Bengal founded by Rani Rashmoni. <stro

q_en: Who among the following has NOT represented India in its Men's Cricket Test team as a wicketkeeper?
e_en: The correct answer is Hanuma Vihari. Hanuma Vihari : He is an Indian international cricketer. He represents Andhra Pradesh in Indian domestic cricket. A right-handed batsman and occasional right-arm off-break bowler. He was a member of the India Under-19 cricket team that won the 2012 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup in Australia.

q_en: In which of the following states is the Telaiya dam located?
e_en: The correct answer is Jharkhand. Telaiya Dam is situated in Jharkhand. It is the first Dam and hydro -Electric power station constructed by Damodar Valley Corporation across the Barakar River, in the Koderma district. The dam is 1200 ft long and 99 ft high situated in an ideal surrounding with a beautiful reservoir in a 36 sq km area. The dam was built with the main object of controlling floods, the hydroelectric station produces 4MW.

q_en: Which of the following rivers originates from Sihawa Mountain?
e_en: The correct answer is Mahanadi. Mahanadi: ​It originates from the Sihawa Mountain in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh. The river originates from an extension of the Eastern Ghats. It flows in Odisha where it joins the Bay of Bengal. Other names of Mahanadi are Kanaknandini, Chitrapalal, Mahasweta, Nilotpala etc. Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi. It is the largest earthen dam in the world.​

q_en: In which of the following years was the Indian Universities Act passed during the tenure of Lord Curzon?
e_en: The correct answer is 1904. Indian University Act 1904 The first provision of this act was that the governing bodies of the universities were to be reconstituted For the Universities of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras, the elected fellows were to be 50 and for the rest of the universities, the number was fixed at 15. This act allowed the Government to appoint a majority of the fellows in a university.

q_en: How many sections are there in the Government of India Act, 1935?
e_en: The correct answer is 321. The government of India act 1935 was passed by the British Parliament in August 1935.With 321 sections and 10 schedules. This was the longest act passed by the British Parliament so far and was later split into two parts viz. Government of India act 1935 and Government of Burma act 1935. The Government of India acts in 1935 derived material from four key sources viz. Report of the Simon Commission, discussions at the third round table conference.

q_en: 1 September marks the beginning of the meteorological _______ in the Southern Hemisphere.
e_en: The correct answer is spring. September Equinox marks is the first day of spring in the southern hemisphere. It is known as the Spring Equinox in the earth’s southern areas (southern hemisphere). An equinox occurs twice in a year one is in March which is known as Spring Equinox and another is in September which is known as Autumn Equinox.

q_en: Kalinga is present-day coastal _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha. Kalinga Kalinga is a historical region of India. It is generally defined as the eastern coastal region between the Mahanadi and the Godavari rivers, although its boundaries have fluctuated with the territory of its rulers. Kalinga, an ancient territorial subdivision of east-central India. It corresponds to present-day northern Telangana, northeastern Andhra Pradesh, most of Odisha, and a portion of Madhya Pradesh states.

q_en: World Alzheimer's Day is observed on _______ globally every year.
e_en: The correct answer is 21 September. World Alzheimer’s Day It is celebrated on September 21 each year. On this day, the world concentrates its efforts on creating awareness of Alzheimer’s disease. The disease is among the most prevalent forms of dementia, a set of disorders that disrupt mental function.

q_en: The Moortidevi award is an Indian literary award presented annually by the ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Bharatiya Jnanpith. The Moortidevi award The Moortidevi Award is

q_en: UPI is a system that powers multiple bank accounts into a single mobile application. What is the full form of UPI?
e_en: The correct answer is Unified Payments Interface. Unified Payments Interface Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is a system that powers multiple bank accounts into a single mobile application (of any participating bank), merging several banking features, seamless fund routing & merchant payments into one hood. It also caters to the “Peer to Peer” collect request which can be scheduled and paid as per requirement and convenience.

q_en:
Which of the following is/are NOT true about revenue receipts?
I. They are receipts of the government which are non-redeemable.
II. They can be claimed from the government under special circumstances.
e_en: The correct answer is Only II. There is a constitutional requirement in India (Article 112) to present before the Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government in respect of every financial year which runs from 1 April to 31 March. This ‘Annual Financial Statement’ constitutes the main budget document. Therefore, the budget comprises of the-Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget.

q_en: The popular ritual of ‘Kanya/Kumari Puja’ is held during which of the following festivals?
e_en: The correct answer is Sharad Navaratri. Sharad Navratri is regarded by many devotees to be the most important one and is also therefore called Maha Navratri. It is celebrated during the Sharad period i.e. beginning of wintertime so it is also referred to as Sharad or Shardiya Navratri. </strong&g

q_en: Tomara Rajputs were defeated in the twelfth century by the Chauhans of ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Ajmer. Tomara Rajputs were defeated in the twelfth century by the Chauhans of Ajmer. The Tomara was an Indian dynasty that ruled parts of present-day Delhi and Haryana during the 9th-12th century. Tomara dynasty: The dynasty ruled India during the 8th-12th century. Their kingdoms were expanded and ruled parts of present-day Delhi and Haryana. Anangpur was the capital.

q_en: The division of powers between the Union and the States is in the ______ Schedule.
e_en: The correct answer is Seventh. The division of powers between the Union and the States is in the Seventh Schedule. Seventh Schedule It contains three lists: Union List, State List and Concurrent List 7th Schedule of Indian Constitution – Union List had 97 subjects. Now, it has 100 subjects. 88th Amendment added a new subject in the Union List called ‘taxes on services.’ The state list has 61 subjects. Earlier, it had 66 items.

q_en: The first Tirthankara of Jainism is believed to be Rishabhanatha, who was born in ____________.
e_en: The correct answer is Ayodhya. The first Tirthankara of Jainism is believed to be Rishabhanatha, who was born in Ayodhya. He was born to the fourteenth and last Kulakara King Nabhi and his Queen Marudevi in Ayodhya. He was also known as Adinatha and Adish Jina. According to Jain tradition, there were 24 Thirthankaras, the first being Rishabhadeva and the last i.e 24th being Mahavira. The Vishnu Purana and the Bhagavat Purana describe Rishabha as an incarnation of Narayana.

q_en: Which of the following is a wildlife sanctuary in north-east India?
e_en: The correct answer is Manas. Manas National Park is also known as Manas Wildlife Sanctuary. It is situated in Assam. This National park is a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site, a Project Tiger reserve, an elephant reserve, and a biosphere reserve in Assam. Manas is famous for its population of wild water buffalo. q_en: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India states that there shall be a special officer for linguistic minorities to be appointed by the President?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 350B. Originally, the Constitution of India did not make any provision with respect to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Later, the States Reorganization Commission (1953-55) made a recommendation in this regard. Accordingly, the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted a new Article 350-B in Part XVII of the Constitution.

q_en: In which of the following states is Arulmigu Kapaleeshwarar Temple located?
e_en: The correct answer is Tamil Nadu. Kapaleeshwarar Temple is an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located in Mylapore, Tamil Nadu. It was built around the 7th century CE in the Dravidian style of temple architecture. Shiva is worshiped as Kapaleeswarar and is represented by the lingam. His consort Parvati is depicted as Karpagambal.

q_en: When is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer observed globally every year?
e_en: The correct answer is 16 September. In 1994, the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 16 September the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer. In 1985, the world’s governments adopted the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer. Under the Convention's Montreal Protocol, governments, scientists, and industry worked together to cut out 99 per cent of all ozone-depleting substances.

q_en: In which of the following years was the Geological Survey of India established?

The current Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) is Shri Asit Saha, who took charge on July 27, 2024 Regional offices of GSI in India are Lucknow, Jaipur, Nagpur, Hyderabad, Shillong and Kolkata.

q_en: Which of the following places in India has the widest difference between day and night temperatures?

This is because of the fact that sand (found in ample quantity in this region) gains and loses heat very quickly. As a result of this phenomenon, there is a wide difference between day and night temperatures in this region. The day temperature may rise to 50°C and drop down to near 15°C the same night. q_en: In the context of banking, which of the following does the letter 'M' stand for in MICR?
e_en: The correct answer is Magnetic. MICR code in the banking stands for Magnetic Ink Character Recognition. MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) code is a code printed on cheques. The embedded code is printed in MICR. It enables the identification of the cheques, which results in faster processing. A MICR code is a 9-digit code.​ It identifies the bank and branch participating in an Electronic Clearing System (ECS).

q_en: Who was the first Indian to circumnavigate the world solo, non-stop?
e_en: The correct answer is Abhilash Tomy. Commander Abhilash Tomy, aged 42, a retired Indian naval officer was the first Indian to circumnavigate non-stop the World solo without any stops in 2013. President Pranab Mukherjee accorded a warm welcome to the Indian Navy's Lt Cdr Abhilash Tomy on his return from over a 150-day voyage. He has sailed around 23,100 nautical miles, crossing the Indian, Southern, Pacific, and Atlantic Oceans.

q_en: 'Slash and burn' agriculture is known as _________ in Mexico and Central America.

The layer of ash after the burning provides the newly-cleared land with a nutrient-rich layer to help fertilize crops. It is also called shifting cultivation. When the soil fertility decreases, the farmers shift and clear a fresh patch of land for cultivation.

q_en: Origin of Species' is a book written by _____ .

q_en: Who was the first Mauryan ruler to have his messages for his subjects and officials engraved on the stone surfaces of polished pillars along with natural rocks?
e_en: The correct answer is Ashoka. Asoka was the first ruler who inscribed his messages on stone surfaces i.e. natural rocks and polished pillars. Most of Ashoks's inscriptions were in Prakrit and were written in Brahmi script. James Prinsep, a British antiquary and colonial administrator was the first person to decipher Ashoka’s edicts. These Ashoka’s inscriptions are the first tangible evidence of Buddhism.

q_en: For which of the following rivers does the longitude reading decrease, as it moves along its course?
e_en: The correct answer is 'Narmada' Narmada: The Narmada river originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in the state of Madhya Pradesh. It flows westward across central India towards the Arabian Sea, ultimately emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat. As the Narmada moves along its course, its longitude readings decrease because it flows from east to west. This east-to-west flow is relatively unique among major rivers in India, which typically flow from north to south or west to east.

q_en: Mirza Hakim was the half-brother of which of these Mughal emperors?

q_en: Who among the following gave the concept of ‘paradox of thrift’?

q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the organisation of village panchayats?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 40. One of the Directive Principles of State Policy enshrined in Article 40 of the Indian Constitution is that the State shall take all necessary steps to organise local panchayats. The state shall grant village panchayats such rights and authority as may be required to allow them to act as self-governing bodies. The key characteristics of Panchayati Raj Institutions must provide them with certainty, consistency, and strength.

q_en: In which of the following states is the Mamallapuram Dance Festival organised?
e_en: The correct answer is Tamil Nadu. Every year, from early January to early February, the Mamallapuram Dance Festival takes place for four weeks in Tamil Nadu. Exponents of Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohiniattam, Odissi, and Kathak gather in this town for this major festival to perform spellbinding performances in Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohini Attam, Odissi, and Kathak.

q_en: Which of the following is the highest mountain of Bhutan?
e_en: The correct answer is Gangkhar Puensum. With an elevation of 7,570 metres (24,836 feet) and a prominence of 2,995 metres, Gangkhar Puensum is Bhutan's highest mountain and the world's highest unclimbed mountain. Its name means "White Peak of the Three Spiritual Brothers." It shares a border with Tibet.

q_en: The natural aging of a lake by nutrient enrichment of its water is called ______.
e_en: The correct answer is eutrophication. When a body of water becomes highly mineralized and nutrient-rich, planktonic algae develop rapidly as a result of this. Eutrophication is the process of excessive growth of planktonic algae in nutrient-rich water. Hypoxia is formed as a result of excessive planktonic algae development, which leads to the death of aquatic animals due to low oxygen levels and the gradual disappearance of the lake.

q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with Uniform Civil Code for citizens?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 44. The Uniform Civil Code is based on the concept of one country, one code that applies to all faith groups. Part 4 of the Indian Constitution, Article 44, specifically mentions the term "Uniform Civil Code." "The State shall seek to ensure for citizens a consistent civil code across the territory of India," states Article 44.

q_en: Who among the following scholar translated Patanjali’s work on grammar into Arabic?
e_en: The correct answer is Al-Biruni. Al-Biruni lived in the eastern Islamic world during an era of unprecedented political instability. He was a servant to more than six princes. Al-Biruni spent years acquiring Sanskrit and studying religious and philosophical writings in the presence of Brahmana priests and academics. Because Al-Biruni was fluent in numerous languages, he was able to compare and translate writings.

q_en: Which of the following is one of the animal motifs found on the cylindrical seal of the Indus region?
e_en: The correct answer is Humped bull. The humped bull is one of the animal motifs found on the cylindrical seal of the Indus region. The humped bull figurine had a molded head that was twisted to the side, and a mold was used to make the head. The body was made by hand, and the head was connected. As with the enormous hollow bull statues, the eyes were crafted with applique pupils.

q_en: ______ is the care and cultivation of wildlands.
e_en: The correct answer is Silviculture. Silviculture is the activity of managing the growth, composition/structure and quality of forests to meet certain goals and objectives, such as timber production. In general, silviculture is the science and art of growing and growing forest crops, based on an understanding of silvix (the study of the life-history and general characteristics of forest trees a

q_en: Kathak exponent and Padma Vibhushan awardee Pt Birju Maharaj was the torchbearer of which gharana of the Lucknow style of Kathak?
e_en: The correct answer is Kalka-Bindadin. Pandit Birju Maharaj was an Indian Kathak dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the Banaras Gharana's "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana. His two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, as well as his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj, were all Kathak dancers. He was also a vocalist who sang Hindustani classical music.

q_en: The Ashoka Chakra Class-II was renamed as ______ in 1967.
e_en: The correct answer is Kirti Chakra. Before 1967, Kirti Chakra was known as Ashok Chakra, Class II. The Kirti Chakra is an Indian military decoration given for gallantry, bravery, or self-sacrifice off the battlefield.</li&

q_en: Which of the following Nobel Laureates has written ‘Cooking to Save Your Life’ which is a book on cooking?
e_en: The correct answer is Abhijit Banerjee. Abhijit Banerjee, an Indian-born American economist and Nobel laureate, has written a new book (cookbook) titled "Cooking to Save Your Life." Juggernaut Books published the book, which was illustrated by Cheyenne Oliver, a French illustrator. In 2019, he, along with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their innovative approach to reducing global poverty.

q_en: Where is the 'Ahom Raja’s Palace' located?
e_en: The correct answer is Assam. The palace of Ahom Raja is a historic structure in Garhgaon, Assam, India. The four-story palace has a dome-shaped ceiling and a chamber on the top floor. Only two of the original four watchtowers remain. On the ground floor of the palace, there are three west-facing halls. For more than four centuries, Gargoan was the Ahoms' main seat.

q_en: In which of the following years did the peasant movement in Bardoli take place?
e_en: The correct answer is 1928. The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was a movement launched by Sardar Vallabhai Patel for the farmers of Bardoli against illegal tax increases during the independence war. On June 12, 1928, the Bardoli Satyagraha took place in Gujarat, India, during the British Raj, and was a major act of civil disobedience and revolt in the Indian Independence Movement.

q_en: From which country did Amazon Prime Video start its first mobile-only plan in the world?
e_en: The correct answer is India. In India, Amazon Prime Video Mobile Edition, a single-user, mobile-only service, was offered at an initial price of 89 rupees per month. The over-the-top platform is launching a mobile-only package in India for the first time. Amazon Prime Video is a subscription video-on-demand over-the-top streaming and renting service operated by Amazon in the United States. It is available as a standalone service or as part of Amazon's Prime membership.

q_en: Khush Mahal within the walls of Warangal Fort, was built in which of the following dynasties?
e_en: The correct answer is Tughlaq. During the reign of Tughlak, the Khush Mahal is claimed to have been built on the location of the Kakatiya palace. It was constructed in the 14th century as an audience hall. The fort has four ornamental gates known as Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, which were once the entrances to a now-destroyed huge Shiva temple. Following the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the Kakatiyan arch was accepted and officially included in Telangana's insignia.

q_en: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following Union Territories has the lowest density of population?
e_en: The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The concentration of individuals within a species in a given geographic location is referred to as population density. Data on population density can be used to calculate demographics and examine interactions with ecosystems, human health, and infrastructure. Population density is usually quoted per square kilometre or square mile.

q_en: Which of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains a list of central and state laws which CANNOT be challenged in courts?
e_en: The correct answer is Ninth Schedule. The Ninth Schedule contains a list of central and state legislation that is not subject to legal challenge. There are now 284 such laws that are immune from judicial review. The blanket immunity given to laws listed in Schedule 9 was affected by a landmark decision made by the Supreme Court of India in the case of IR Coelho vs. State of Tamil Nadu (2007).

q_en: Which of the following forts is located in Rajasthan?
e_en: The correct answer is Mehrangarh Fort. Mehrangarh Fort is a 1,200-acre (486-hectare) fort located in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India. It was constructed in 1459 by Rajput ruler Rao Jodha, though most of the existing structure is from the 17th century. The chhatri of Kirat Singh Soda, a soldier who died defending Mehrangarh, is located to the left of the fort.

q_en: Who among the following has written the book ‘Manohar Parrikar - Off the Record’?
e_en: The correct answer is Waman S Prabhu. Pramod Sawant, the Chief Minister of Goa, released book titled "Manohar Parrikar- Off the Record." Waman Subha Prabhu, a distinguished journalist, penned the book. This book is a collection of memories from Mr Prabhu, who was with late Parrikar throughout his life's journey.

q_en: Ozone depletion from the atmosphere becomes the reason for causing which of the following diseases?
e_en: The correct answer is Skin cancer. The gradual thinning of the Earth's ozone layer in the upper atmosphere caused by the discharge of chemical compounds containing gaseous chlorine or bromine from industry and other human activities is referred to as ozone depletion. The thinning is mainly noticeable over Antarctica and in the polar regions.

q_en: Which of the following rivers has its source in the Sumeru glacier above the Kedarnath temple?
e_en: The correct answer is Mandakini. The River Mandakini has its source in the Sumeru glacier above the Kedarnath Temple. The Mandakini River is a tributary of the Alaknanda River in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. The river emerges from the Chorabari Glacier and travels for around 81 kilometres between the Rudraprayag and Sonprayag districts. At Sonprayag, the river merges with the Songanga and runs past the Hindu temple Madhyamaheshwar in Ukhimath.

q_en: Gombe Habba is a famous festival of which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Karnataka. Every year, during Dasara/Navaratri, enthusiastic persons celebrate Gombe Habba, or doll festival in Karnataka. The Festival of Dolls entails gathering a diverse collection of dolls, displaying them on a multi-stage platform, and inviting people to view them. Wood is a frequent material for dolls. Metal, plastic, and clay dolls can also be used.

q_en: According to the Jaina tradition, Mahavira was preceded by how many other teachers or Trithankaras?
e_en: The correct answer is 23. Mahavira is erroneously called the founder of Jainism, but Jains believe that the 23 previous Tirthankaras also espoused it. Parshvanatha, also called Parshva was the 23rd Tirthankara (&l

q_en: Loor is the famous dance from which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Haryana. Loor dance is a popular traditional folk dance from Haryana, a state in northern India. It's a way for the locals to express joy and sadness, just like any other folk dance. It is highly famous in Haryana's Bangar and Bagar regions. It is held in the month of 'Phalguna,' which corresponds to the months of February and March in the Gregorian calendar. The dance also heralds the arrival of spring and the planting of rabi crops.

q_en: Yarlung Tsangpo river which rises in Tibet, popularly known as ______in India.
e_en: The correct answer is Brahmaputra. The Yarlung Tsangpo, commonly known as the Yarlung Zangbo, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River in China's Tibet Autonomous Region. It is Tibet's longest river and China's fifth-longest river.

q_en: Starting from which of the following years did Raja Ram Mohan Roy publish the Sambad Kaumudi?
e_en: The correct answer is 1821. Ram Mohan Roy published Sambad Kaumudi, a Bengali weekly newspaper, from Kolkata in the first part of the nineteenth century. It was a well-known pro-Reformist periodical that actively advocated for the Sati Pratha's removal.

q_en: In which of the following years was the final Constitution adopted in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 1949. The Indian Constitution was passed and adopted by the assembly on November 26, 1949. The Constitution had 395 articles and 8 schedules when it was adopted, and it was nearly 145,000 words long, making it the longest national constitution ever. The members of the Constituent Assembly debated every article in the Consti

q_en: Which of the following revolutionary freedom fighters was assassinated by Abdul Rashid?
e_en: The correct answer is Swami Shraddhanand. Swami Shraddhanand, also known as Mahatma Munshi Ram Vij, was an Indian nationalist and Arya Samaj sannyasi who spread Dayananda Saraswati's teachings. This includes the development of educational institutions such as the Gurukul Kangri University, as well as a vital part in the Hindu reform movements of the Sangathan (consolidation and organization) and Shuddhi (purification) in the 1920s.

q_en: Which of the following States / Union Territories has the highest literacy rate according to Census 2011?
e_en: The correct answer is Lakshadweep. According to Census 2011, Lakshadweep, with a literacy rate of 92.28%, is the Union Territory with the highest literacy rate in India. The female literacy rate of Lakshadweep is 88.25%. Kerala ranks the highest in terms of literacy rate with a 94.00% literacy rate.

q_en: The word ______ implies that the head of the state in India shall be an elected person and shall hold office for a fixed term.
e_en: The correct answer is Republic. The word Republic implies that the head of the state in India shall be an elected person and shall hold office for a fixed term. The term Republic indicates that the head of the state is elected by the people directly or indirectly. In India, the President is the head of the state and he is elected indirectly by the people.

q_en: Which of the following festivals of Andhra Pradesh is celebrated on the third day of Krishna Paksh of Aashvijam?
e_en: The correct answer is ​Atla Tadde. Atla Tadde is a festival of Andhra Pradesh that is celebrated on the third day of Krishna Paksh of Aashvijam. Atla Tadde is a traditional festival celebrated by both unmarried and married Hindu women of Andhra Pradesh for getting a husband or for the health and long life of their husbands. Rotiyaan ki eid or Rottela Panduga is an annual three-day urs(festival) held at Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore in Andhra Pradesh, India.

q_en: In which of the following years was the Satyagraha Ashram founded by Mahatma Gandhi?
e_en: The correct answer is 1915. Satyagraha Ashram at Ahmedabad is the place where Mahatma Gandhi lived after he returned from South Africa in 1915. The “Satyagraha Ashrama” was founded by Mahatama Gandhi at Kocharab near Ahmedabad in the year 1915. Later in 1917, the ashram was shifted to Sabarmati and came to be known as the “Sabarmati Ashram”. The ashram was relocated because Gandhiji wanted to carry out agricultural activities.

q_en: At which of the following places did Lord Buddha attain Mahaparinirvana?
e_en: The correct answer is Kushinagar. Gautam Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana in Kushinagar (in present-day Uttar Pradesh). Mahaparinirvana usually means the ultimate state of Nirvana (everlasting, highest peace and happiness) attained by an Awakened Being. Kushinagar is the final resting place of Gautam Buddha. It is a Buddhist pilgrimage site.

q_en: Lingaraja Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in Bhubaneshwar, was built during which of the following dynasties?
e_en: The correct answer is Somavamsi dynasty. Lingaraja Temple was built in the 11th century AD by King Jajati Keshari of the Somavanshi dynasty. It is built in red stone. ​The Lingaraja Temple is built in the Deula style that has four components- Vimana (structure containing the sanctum) Jagamohana (assembly hall) Natamandira (festival hall) Bhoga-mandapa (hall of offerings)

q_en: Who among the following wrote the book ‘Redesign the World: A Global Call to Action’?
e_en: The correct answer is Sam Pitroda. Sam Pitroda wrote the book ‘Redesign the World: A Global Call to Action’. Dr. Sam Pitodra is better known as "The father of India's communication revolution". He is a policymaker, investor, and entrepreneur. Presently, he is the chairman of India's National Knowledge Commission (NKC), besides being the Chairman and CEO of World-Tel and the founder and CEO of C-SAM, Inc. In 1992, he was also an advisor to the United Nations.

q_en: Wildlife Week is celebrated in India with the aim to preserve the fauna. In which of the following months is it celebrated?
e_en: The correct answer is October.

q_en: Panthi folk dance belongs to which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Chattisgarh. Panthi, one of the important dance forms in Chattisgarh is the folk dance of Chattisgarh. It is mainly performed by the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh. Saila Dance, Karma, Sua Nacha, and Gendi are the other important folk dances of Chattisgarh.

q_en: Gurudongmar Lake is located in which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Sikkim. Gurudongmar Lake is one of the highest lakes in the world and India, situated at an altitude of 5,154 m (16,900 ft), in the Indian state of Sikkim. It is considered sacred to the Buddhists, Sikhs, and Hindus. The lake is named after Guru Padmasambhava (the founder of Tibetan Buddhism). Cholamu Lake and Tsonmgo Lake are located in Sikkim.

q_en: Who among the following, with Michelle Li, has been nominated as the athlete ambassador for the International Olympic Committee’s (IOC) ‘Believe in Sport’ campaign?
e_en: The correct answer is PV Sindhu.

q_en: According to the Constitution of India, who among the following is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
e_en: The correct answer is Vice President. Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. ​The term of the Vice President of India is 5 years. The oath of office to the Vice President is administered by the President. The Vice President of India gives his resignation letter to the President.​

e_en: The correct answer is 1906-1907. In 1906-07 Mahatma Gandhi led his first Satyagraha in South Africa protesting against the Asiatic Registration Act. In 1906, he led the first Civil Disobedience Movement (Satyagraha) against Asiatic Ordinance in Transvaal. In 1907, he led a Satyagraha against Compulsory Registration and Passes for Asians (The Black Act) in Transvaal.

q_en: Which of the following gases is NOT included in greenhouse gases?
e_en: The correct answer is Nitrogen. The major greenhouse gases are: Water Vapour - causes about 36% - 70% of the greenhouse effect Carbon dioxide (CO2) which causes 9 - 26% Methane (CH4) causes 4 - 9% Ozone (O3) Nitrous Oxide Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) Hence, Nitrogen is the correct answer.

q_en: In which of the following countries is the Sri Pada mountain located?
e_en: The correct answer is Sri Lanka. Sri Pada mountain is located in Sri Lanka. Sri Pada is the second highest mountain in Sri Lanka. It is also known as Adam's Peak. It is a 2,243 m tall conical mountain located in central Sri Lanka.

q_en: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi visit Noakhali and other riot-torn areas to stop communal violence?
e_en: The correct answer is 1946. In 1946, Mahatma Gandhi visited Noakhali and other riot-torn areas to stop communal violence. The riots in Noakhali took place in the backdrop of unrest due to the demand for partition by the Muslim league. This happened in Noakhali, a place in then Bengal(now in Bangladesh) in the year 1946. Gandhiji visited the place to advocate his message of non-violence. A large scale of atrocities was committed against the members of the Hindu community.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a rabi crop?
e_en: The correct answer is Cotton. Rabi crops or rabi harvest are agricultural crops that are sown in winter and harvested in the spring in India. Some example of Rabi crops is wheat, barley, gram, peas, mustard, rapeseed and linseed. Hence Cotton is NOT a rabi crop. States from the north and northwestern parts such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.

q_en: Subarnarekha River basin is located in which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Jharkhand. The Subarnarekha originates from the Ranchi Plateau in Jharkhand forming the boundary between West Bengal and Odisha in its lower course. It joins the Bay of Bengal forming an estuary between the Ganga and Mahanadi deltas. Its total length is 395 km.

q_en: Sindhudurg Fort is located in which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Maharashtra. Sindhudurg Fort is located in Maharashtra. It was built by Shivaji in 1664. Its main architect was Hirojee Indulkar. The main objective to build this fort was to counter the rising influence of foreign( English, Dutch, French, Portuguese) merchants. It was built on Khurte Island. Now it is controlled by the Government of India.

q_en: On which of the following days is the World Asthma Day organised annually by the World Health Organization's collaborative organization - Global Initiative for Asthma?
e_en: The correct answer is 5 May.

q_en: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in Jharkhand during the spring season in the worship of the village deity who is considered to be the protector of the tribes and the Saal trees get new flowers on their branches?
e_en: The correct answer is Sarhul. Sarhul festival, the most popular tribal celebration across the Jharkhand region, was celebrated on 4 April 2022. Sarhul means worshipping trees. It is celebrated by the tribal communities of the local Sarna religion, most notably by the Munda, Ho, and Oraon tribes. It is celebrated at the beginning of spring every year in the first month of the Hindu calendar, on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of ‘Chaitra’.

q_en: Which of the following dance forms of Nagaland is performed as preparation for a hunting expedition?
e_en: The correct answer is Sadal Kekai. Sadal Kekai dance is performed by the Kuki tribe. This dance form of Nagaland is performed as preparation for a hunting expedition.

q_en: According to which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution shall the law declared by the Supreme Court be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 141. Article 141 of the Indian constitution: It states that "Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts, the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India". *Hence option A is correct.* ​The Supreme Court was established on 26th January 1950. e_en: The correct answer is 1739.

e_en: The correct answer is 26. 26 signs used to be part of the longest inscription found on Harappan seals. Indus-script adherents sometimes claim (usually quickly, and without much discussion) that the longest Indus 'inscription' is 26 signs long.

e_en: The correct answer is Dadra and Nagar Haveli. According to Census 2011, Dadra and Nagar Haveli have the top population growth rate. The growth of population is the change in the number of people living in a particular area between two points in time. Its rate is expressed in percentages.

q_en: 'Resolved: Uniting Nations in a Divided World' is a memoir of who among the following former UN Secretary Generals?
e_en: The correct answer is Ban Ki-Moon. Former United Nations Secretary-General Ban-Ki-moon's autobiography is titled "Resolved: Uniting Nations in a Divided World." It includes the author's life experiences and obstacles, as well as details of his time at the United Nations (UN). He served as the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations from January 2007 to December 2016.

q_en: The Advocate General of each state of India is appointed by:
o_en: the Chief Minister of the State
e_en: The correct answer is the Governor of the State. A state government's advocate general is a legal advisor. The post was formed by the Indian Constitution (see Article 165) and is equivalent to the position of Attorney General for India at the federal level. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor of each state and must be eligible to serve as a High Court judge.

q_en: In 1943, some of the younger leaders in which district of Maharashtra set up a parallel government (Prati Sarkar), with volunteer corps (Seba dals) and village units (Tufan dals )?
e_en: The correct answer is Satara. The Satara Parallel Government in Maharashtra, which fought British control from August 1943 to May 1946, was a legendary chapter in India's historic freedom war. It, like the parallel administrations in Bengal's Midnapore, Bihar's Bhagalpur, Uttar Pradesh's Ballia, and Odisha's Basudevpur, was an armed outgrowth of the 1942 Quit India movement.

q_en: As per India Census 2011, which of the 22 languages specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India is spoken by least number of people?
e_en: The correct answer is Sanskrit. In all, 13 of the 22 scheduled languages had at least 1% of the population reporting them as their mother tongue. Except for Sanskrit, each of the 21 listed languages has at least 10 lakh people reporting it as their mother tongue.</li

q_en: The official name (in English) of Bangladesh is:
e_en: The correct answer is People's Republic of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is a country in South Asia that is officially known as the People's Republic of Bangladesh. It is the world's seventh most populous country, with almost 163 million people living in an area of either 148,460 square kilometres or 147,570 square kilometres, making it one of the world's most densely inhabited countries.

q_en: While adopting the Constitution of India in 1949, by which Article of the Constitution of India, the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or supplementing the latter Act, EXCEPT the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was repealed?
e_en: The correct answer is 395. Article 395 repeals the Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the Government of India Act of 1935, as well as all amendments and supplements to the latter Act, except the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act of 1949. The Government of India Act, 1935, abolished the dyarchy established by the Government of India Act, 1919, and established a Federation of India consisting of British India provinces and some or all of the Princely states.

q_en: In which of the following Indian states were the remains of the ancient Vikramshila University discovered?
e_en: The correct answer is Bihar. Vikramshila is an ancient site located 40 km away from the Bhagalpur city of Bihar. The small town is famous for housing Vikramshila University, which was built under the guidance of Dharmapala, a Pala King of the 8th century AD. Situated on top of the hills along the banks of the river Ganges, the university became a learning centre of Tantric Buddhism.

q_en: In which of the following countries did the former prime minister Lal Bahadur Shastri die?
e_en: The correct answer is Uzbekistan. On the 11th of January 1966, Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent, Uzbekistan (then Soviet Union), one day after signing a peace accord ending the 1965 Indo-Pakistan War. He was hailed as a national hero, and the Vijay Ghat memorial was named for him.

q_en: Ugadi Pachadi is a famous dish that is associated with the Ugadi festival of south India. How many different types of ingredients does it contain?

After presenting it to the gods, it is the first dish eaten at the Ugadi festival. Apart from the health advantages of this festive drink, Ugadi Pachadi also means accepting life in all of its forms.

q_en: Mohiniyattam dance emotes a play through dancing and singing where the song is customarily in which of the following languages?

Traditions never remain static; they change over time as a result of shifting aesthetic and social tastes. Female artists do Mohiniattam, a solo performance.

q_en: Who among the following musicians was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999?
e_en: The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar. Pandit Ravi Shankar, a sitar player, composer, and founder of the National Orchestra of India, received India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999. Born in Benares (now Varanasi) in 1920, Shankar passed away in San Diego, California, in 2012.

q_en: Ganesh Chaturthi is observed in ________ month of Hindu calendar.
e_en: The correct answer is Bhadrapada. In Hinduism, Ganesh Chaturthi is a ten-day celebration commemorating the birth of the elephant-headed god Ganesha, who is known as the knowledge and prosperity god. It starts on the fourth day, or chathurthi, of Bhadrapada, the sixth month in the Hindu calendar, which runs from August to September. Ganesha idols are set up on elevated platforms in houses or in ornately decorated outside tents before the beginning of the celebration.

q_en: Who among the following was the author of the book ‘Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi’?

q_en: Which Indian musician’s autobiography is titled ‘Raga Mala’?

q_en: Which of the following is a Rabi crop in Northern India?
e_en: The correct answer is Mustard. Mustard is a Rabi crop in Northern India. Mustard is categorized as a Rabi crop, typically sown during the period from October to November and harvested between March and April. This oilseed crop flourishes in dry and cool climates, necessitating cooler temperatures for optimal growth. It is extensively cultivated in India, with yellow varieties predominantly cultivated in regions such as Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.

q_en: Which of the following pair of dances belongs to Kerala?
e_en: The correct answer is Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Kathakali and Mohiniyattam pair of dances belongs to Kerala. Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dance forms originating from Kerala, India. Kathakali is renowned for its theatrical elements, including elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, expressive face masks, and ornate ornaments. Mohiniyattam is characterized by its graceful movements, predominantly performed by women.

q_en: Under _____ a new policy of “paramountcy” was initiated. In this policy the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.

In this policy the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states. Lord Hastings, serving as the Governor-General of India from 1813 to 1823, implemented the policy of paramountcy.

q_en: Which union territory has the highest sex ratio value according to the 2011 census?
e_en: The correct answer is Puducherry. As per the 2011 census data, Puducherry boasts the highest sex ratio among all union territories, with 1037 females for every 1000 males. Following closely behind are Lakshadweep (946), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (878), Kashmir (883), and Sikkim (889), which also exhibit relatively high sex ratios. Conversely, the union territories with the lowest sex ratios include Daman and Diu (618), Dadra and Nagar Haveli (775), and Chandigarh (818).

q_en: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, which is dedicated to Shiva and was constructed in 999 by the Chandela dynasty, is an example of which of the following styles of architecture?
e_en: The correct answer is Nagara style. The Kandariya Mahadeva temple exemplifies Nagara-style architecture, also known as the idol Nagara style, and is renowned as one of India's finest temples. It stands as a prominent example of central Indian architecture and follows the Panchayatana style, akin to Kalinga architecture in its arrangement. Commissioned by King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty in 999 CE, the temple is dedicated to the deity Shiva.

q_en: Who among the following was the founder and director of the ‘Darpana Academy of Performing Arts’, an institute that focuses on training students in dance, drama, music and puppetry, in the city of Ahmedabad?
e_en: The correct answer is Mrinalini Sarabhai. Mrinalini Sarabhai was the founder and director of the ‘Darpana Academy of Performing Arts’, an institute that focuses on training students in dance, drama, music and puppetry, in the city of Ahmedabad. Mrinalini Sarabhai and Vikram Sarabhai founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in 1949, situated in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

q_en: From the given alternatives, identify the dwarf planet.
e_en: The correct answer is Pluto. Pluto, a dwarf planet situated in the Kuiper Belt, orbits the Sun beyond Neptune's orbit. Discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, Pluto was initially regarded as the ninth planet. However, in 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet. Despite being the largest known trans-Neptunian object by volume, Pluto is less massive than Eris.

q_en: Which of the following is the oldest text of ancient India?
e_en: The correct answer is Rig Veda. The Rigveda stands as the oldest known text of ancient India, penned in Sanskrit circa 1500 BC. As the earliest among the Vedas, the sacred scriptures of Hinduism, it comprises 1,028 hymns partitioned into 10 sections known as mandalas. These hymns venerate Rigvedic deities and are frequently recited during religious rituals. Notably, the Rigveda holds the distinction of being one of the oldest extant texts in any Indo-European language.

q_en: The Jhelum River rises from which of the following sources?
e_en: The correct answer is Spring at Verinag. The Jhelum River originates from the Verinag spring situated in the Kashmir Valley, nestled at the base of the Pir Panjal range in Anantnag. It traverses through Srinagar and Wular Lake before exiting into Pakistan via a narrow gorge. As the westernmost of the five rivers in the Punjab region, the Jhelum spans a length of 725 kilometers.

q_en: How many Fundamental Duties are there in the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is 11. The Indian Constitution enshrines 11 fundamental duties for citizens, delineated in Article 51-A. Originally, the Constitution solely included fundamental rights without any mention of fundamental duties. However, in 1976, the 42nd Amendment Act introduced 10 fundamental duties. Subsequently, in 2002, the 86th Constitutional Amendment appended an 11th fundamental duty.

q_en: The executive power of the Union in India rests with _______.
e_en: The correct answer is President. As per the Indian Constitution, the executive authority of the Union is vested in the President, who may exercise it directly or through subordinate officers. However, the practical exercise of executive power is primarily conducted by the Council of Ministers, under the leadership of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister, a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, must meet certain eligibility criteria.

q_en: There shall be a _______ with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President of India.
e_en: The correct answer is Council of Ministers. There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President of India. Article 74(1) of the Constitution of India stipulates that the President of India shall be assisted and advised by a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The President is mandated to act in accordance with the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers.

q_en: What is the distance between the two goal posts in a football match?
e_en: The correct answer is 7.32 m. The distance between the two goal posts in a football match is 7.32 m. In a football match, the goalposts are the vertical structures located at each end of the playing field. These goalposts are used as targets for scoring goals. The distance between the two goal posts is standardized according to the Laws of the Game, which govern football matches worldwide.

q_en: Which is the only mangrove habitat in the world for the species Panthera Tigris?
e_en: The Correct answer is Sunderbans. The Sundarbans, located on the delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers in the Bay of Bengal, is the largest contiguous mangrove forest in the world. The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and represents an excellent example of ongoing ecological processes. It is known for its rich biodiversity, including 260 bird species, the Bengal tiger, and other threatened species like the estuarine crocodile and the Indian python.

q_en: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel is known as:
e_en: The Correct answer is Esker. Eskers are long, narrow winding ridges of alternately sorted material comprised of boulders and clay found in lowland areas. They are formed by fluvioglacial deposition. They are ridges made of sands and gravels, deposited by glacial meltwater flowing through tunnels within and underneath glaciers, or through meltwater channels on top of glaciers.

q_en: The Principal of a Sanskrit College who represented a blend of Indian and Western culture was __________.

q_en: The Tomb of Razia Sultan in the state of Haryana is made of which building material?

q_en: Initially who among the following were subordinate to the Chalukyas of Karnataka?
e_en: The correct answer is Rashtrakutas. The Rashtrakutas initially served as vassals to the Chalukyas of Karnataka before eventually establishing their own dynasty in the Deccan region of South India. Dantidurga, a subordinate chief of the Chalukyas, founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty. In the mid-eighth century, Dantidurga overthrew his Chalukya overlords and solidified his rule by performing the hiranya-garbha ritual, symbolizing his ascension to Kshatriya status.

q_en: Forest Research Institute, Dehradun was established as Imperial Forest Research Institute. In which year was it established as “Imperial Forest Research Institute”?
e_en: The correct answer is 1906. The Forest Research Institute (FRI) in Dehradun, India, traces its origins back to 1878 when it was established as the Forest School of Dehradun. Later, in 1906, it was reconstituted as the Imperial Forest Research Institute. FRI serves as a premier natural resource service training institute for the Indian Forest Service and State Forest Service.

q_en: Which of the following players is associated with billiards?
e_en: The correct answer is Pankaj Advani. Pankaj Arjan Advani is an Indian billiards and professional snooker player.
